---
title: "FWB intervals for conditional infit MSQ"
subtitle: "Coverage of the population MSQ, item by item and simultaneously"
author: "Magnus Johansson"
date: today
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(knitr)
})
fs <- list.files("fwb_msq_coverage", pattern = "_n[0-9]+[.]rds$",
                 full.names = TRUE)
L <- lapply(fs, readRDS)
d <- bind_rows(L) |>
  mutate(role = case_when(cond == "null" ~ "null",
                          misfit ~ "misfitting",
                          TRUE ~ "fitting, others misfit"),
         role = factor(role, levels = c("null", "fitting, others misfit",
                                        "misfitting")),
         cond = factor(cond, levels = c("null", "xdim50_k1", "xdim15_k3",
                                        "xdim75_k3")))
B <- unique(vapply(L, function(x) attr(x, "B"), numeric(1)))
minutes <- sum(vapply(L, function(x) attr(x, "minutes"), numeric(1)))
failed <- sum(vapply(L, function(x) length(attr(x, "failed")), integer(1)))
kb <- function(x, ...) kable(x, ...)
```

## Purpose

An effect-size floor on infit judges each item by an interval for its
population MSQ against a band of practical fit, $[1 - \delta, 1 + \delta]$,
instead of testing MSQ = 1. That needs an interval for the observed MSQ under
the data as they are, not under the null. The fractional weighted bootstrap
(FWB) gives every respondent a random positive weight with mean 1, refits the
model by CML with those weights, and recomputes infit. Its percentile interval
reflects the sampling variability of the observed MSQ, including the
re-estimation of the thresholds, and nobody drops out of a draw, so no
category empties.

This note checks whether the intervals cover the population MSQ for three
kinds of item: items under a true Rasch model, misfitting items, and fitting
items distorted by the cascade when other items misfit. It also checks
simultaneous intervals that use one max-type constant over all items, the
infit analogue of Q3max*. The simulation is `fwb_msq_coverage.R`.

## Design

- **Datasets.** Regenerated from `conditional_rmsd_partA.qmd` with its seeds:
  20 dichotomous items evenly spaced on [-2, 2], theta ~ N(0, 1.5^2), and
  misfitting items that respond to a second dimension. Each dataset was
  checked against Part A's cached infit.
- **Conditions.** Null; one misfitting item at rho = .50; three misfitting
  items at rho = .15 (the strongest cascade) and at rho = .75 (subtle misfit).
- **Sample sizes.** 500, 2,000, 5,000. 200 datasets per cell.
- **FWB.** `r B` draws per dataset, exponential weights normalised to mean 1,
  weighted CML refit with `psychotools::pcmodel()`, infit from the conditional
  moments with the same weights.
- **Intervals.** Per item, the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of the draws.
  Simultaneous: in each draw take the largest standardised departure over
  items, $\max_i |\text{MSQ}_{bi} - \text{MSQ}_i| / \text{SD}_i$, and use its
  95th percentile $c$ as one constant for all items, giving
  $\text{MSQ}_i \pm c \cdot \text{SD}_i$.
- **Target.** Each item's population MSQ, its Part A mean at n = 20,000
  (300 datasets). Its Monte Carlo SE is about .0005.

The Monte Carlo SE of a 95 percent coverage rate is 1.5 points for one item
over 200 datasets. Rates pooled over items are more precise but not
independent, since items share datasets.

## Checks

```{r checks}
d |>
  group_by(cond, n) |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(rep),
            max_match_error = signif(max(match_err), 2),
            min_draws_ok = min(draws_ok), .groups = "drop") |>
  kb()
```

`r failed` datasets failed. About `r round(minutes)` minutes on 10 cores.

## Coverage, item by item

Share of items whose interval contains the population MSQ (%), by kind of
item. Nominal is 95.

```{r coverage}
d |>
  group_by(role, cond, n) |>
  summarise(percentile = 100 * mean(pop >= lo & pop <= hi),
            simultaneous = 100 * mean(pop >= slo & pop <= shi),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = n, values_from = c(percentile, simultaneous),
              names_glue = "{.value} n={n}") |>
  kb(digits = 1)
```

Coverage of the misfitting items one by one, since they differ in targeting
(0, -1 and -2 logits in the three-item conditions).

```{r coverage-misfit}
d |>
  filter(misfit) |>
  group_by(cond, item, n) |>
  summarise(pop = mean(pop),
            percentile = 100 * mean(pop >= lo & pop <= hi),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = n, values_from = percentile,
              names_prefix = "n = ") |>
  kb(digits = c(0, 0, 3, 1, 1, 1))
```

## Simultaneous coverage

Share of datasets in which every item's simultaneous interval contains its
population MSQ (%). Nominal is 95. The mean of $c$ is shown for reference
(1.96 would be the per-item constant).

```{r simultaneous}
d |>
  group_by(cond, n, rep) |>
  summarise(all = all(pop >= slo & pop <= shi), cmax = first(cmax),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(cond, n) |>
  summarise(all_covered = 100 * mean(all), mean_c = mean(cmax),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  kb(digits = c(0, 0, 1, 2))
```

## Where misses come from

Coverage can fail because the observed MSQ is biased at that n, or because
the FWB spread is too narrow. The table compares the mean observed MSQ with
the population value, and the mean FWB SD with the SD of the observed MSQ
over datasets, which is its real sampling SD at that n.

```{r spread}
d |>
  group_by(role, cond, n, item) |>
  summarise(bias = mean(obs) - first(pop), true_sd = sd(obs),
            fwb_sd = mean(fwb_sd), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(role, cond, n) |>
  summarise(mean_abs_bias = mean(abs(bias)), max_abs_bias = max(abs(bias)),
            sd_ratio = mean(fwb_sd / true_sd), .groups = "drop") |>
  kb(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 4, 4, 2))
```

A ratio near 1 means the FWB spread matches the real one.

## The floor in practice

Decisions with the simultaneous intervals against a band $[1 - \delta,
1 + \delta]$, for two illustrative values of $\delta$. These are not
recommendations, since $\delta$ should come from impact. An item's population
value is "within tolerance" when $|\text{MSQ} - 1| < \delta$. The table gives
the share of items with each decision (%).

```{r floor}
expand_grid(delta = c(0.05, 0.10)) |>
  group_by(delta) |>
  group_modify(function(x, key) {
    dl <- key$delta
    d |>
      mutate(truth = ifelse(abs(pop - 1) < dl, "within tolerance",
                            "beyond tolerance"),
             decision = case_when(slo >= 1 - dl & shi <= 1 + dl ~ "inside",
                                  shi < 1 - dl | slo > 1 + dl ~ "outside",
                                  TRUE ~ "undecided"))
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  count(delta, cond, role, truth, n, decision, name = "k") |>
  group_by(delta, cond, role, truth, n) |>
  mutate(items = sum(k), pct = 100 * k / sum(k)) |>
  select(-k) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = decision, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(delta = sprintf("%.2f", delta)) |>
  select(delta, cond, role, truth, n, items, any_of(c("inside", "undecided",
                                                      "outside"))) |>
  arrange(delta, cond, role, truth, n) |>
  kb(digits = 1)
```

For comparison, the share of fitting items that a test against MSQ = 1 would
flag with these same simultaneous intervals (interval excludes 1), in the
conditions where other items misfit:

```{r test-vs-1}
d |>
  filter(role == "fitting, others misfit") |>
  group_by(cond, n) |>
  summarise(flagged_vs_1 = 100 * mean(slo > 1 | shi < 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = n, values_from = flagged_vs_1,
              names_prefix = "n = ") |>
  kb(digits = 1)
```

## Interpretation

Written 2026-10-12 after the run. 2,400 datasets, none failed, every dataset
identical to Part A (largest difference in infit 1.3e-13).

**1. The FWB spread matches the real sampling spread.** The mean FWB SD over
the SD of the observed MSQ across datasets is 0.97 to 1.03 in every cell with
many items behind it, for null, cascade-affected and misfitting items alike.
The two single-item cells (one misfitting item at rho = .50) give 0.90 to
1.08, where the empirical SD itself rests on 200 values. The observed MSQ is
nearly unbiased for its population value, with a mean absolute bias of .001 to
.004 and at most .007. So FWB does what the floor needs: it measures how
uncertain the observed MSQ is, under the data as they are.

**2. Per-item coverage is close to nominal, slightly under.** The percentile
interval covers the population MSQ for 93.6 to 95.0 percent of items in the
pooled rows, and 89.5 to 95.5 percent for single misfitting items, where the
Monte Carlo SE is 1.5 points. The shortfall of about one point is consistent
with estimating 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles from 200 draws, which makes the
interval slightly too short. More draws, or an SD-based interval (observed MSQ plus or minus 1.96 FWB SDs),
would remove most of it.

**3. Simultaneous coverage is close to nominal.** The share of datasets with
every item covered is 91.0 to 95.5 percent (mean about 93.5). The constant $c$
is about 3.0 at every n, close to the Bonferroni value for 20 items (3.02),
because the items' departures are nearly independent across draws. With
$c$ from 200 draws its 95th percentile is noisy, and B = 1,000 would be the
first thing to try before calling the shortfall real.

**4. The floor stops the cascade.** With three strongly misfitting items
(rho = .15), the fitting items have population MSQ about 0.92. A test against
MSQ = 1, using these same simultaneous intervals, flags them at 11, 59 and
94 percent at n = 500, 2,000 and 5,000. With $\delta = .10$ the floor flags
none of them at any n. They are mostly undecided, because 0.92 lies near the
boundary at 0.90, and the share cleared as inside grows with n (0 to 31
percent). The misfitting items in the same datasets are declared outside in
83, 100 and 100 percent.

**5. The floor turns large n into a positive finding.** Under a true Rasch
model, with $\delta = .10$, items are cleared as practically fitting in 0, 64
and 99.8 percent of cases at n = 500, 2,000 and 5,000. No null item was ever
declared outside. A test cannot give this kind of result.

**6. Small misfit near the boundary stays undecided.** At rho = .75 the
misfitting items have population MSQ 1.09 to 1.14. With $\delta = .10$, the
two above 1.10 are declared outside in 0.2, 2.8 and 18 percent and are
otherwise undecided. The one at 1.09 is never cleared and is falsely declared
outside in at most 1 percent. Undecided is the honest answer for an item
within a few hundredths of the tolerance.

**7. The choice of $\delta$ sets the sample size the floor needs.** With
$\delta = .05$ the simultaneous half-width (about 3 SDs, .048 at n = 5,000)
is as wide as the band, so even null items are cleared only 12 percent of the
time at n = 5,000, and the cascade items at 0.92 count as beyond tolerance
and are declared outside in up to 10 percent. A narrower band needs a larger
sample before it can clear anything. For 20 dichotomous items, n = 5,000
supports a band of about $\pm .10$ and n = 2,000 only partly.

**Limits.** Dichotomous items, 20 items, normal theta, second-dimension
misfit only. B = 200 draws. The values of $\delta$ are illustrations, not
recommendations. In use, $\delta$ should come from impact, and the shortfall
in simultaneous coverage should be rechecked with more draws.
